title: Revenge Game Denied: Alan Hangs 143.66 on the Dawgs While Mekhi's Bench Outscores the Margin
dek: Team Pillbert rolls to a fourth straight win in the trade-bowl rematch, Jordan finally gets on the board in a 50-point rout, and No Banner only HULK climbs to 55% title odds while Randy's season sputters.
body: Week 5 handed Mekhi the revenge game the whole league had circled, and Alan walked out of it with the week's highest score. Team Pillbert won 143.66 to 108.44 at the Dawgs, behind Jahmyr Gibbs, who blew past a 24.57 projection with 35.2 points. The trade subplot came out exactly backward from the scoreboard: Justin Jefferson debuted for Alan with 15.8, while Davante Adams (19.6) and Ashton Jeanty (9.2) combined for 28.8 in Mekhi's lineup. Mekhi won the head-to-head of the trade by 13 points and lost the game by 35.22, which is the most Team Pillbert thing that could have happened.

The real damage was self-inflicted. Mekhi started Tyler Shough, who finished with -0.16 on a 16.51 projection, while Jayden Daniels sat on the bench and scored 32.26. That swap alone would have cut the margin to about 2.8 points, and Christian Watson's 29.3 was also parked on the bench. For a guy who probably knows more football than anyone in this league, leaving 61.56 points of bench production next to a negative quarterback is a lineup call that will be replayed at every draft. The Dawgs fall to 1-4 with 25% playoff odds.

Meanwhile, Jordan is 1-4, and that is a celebration. Counting or not Counting GV beat Ghostu-Spider SZN 119.68 to 69.14 as a 43% home underdog, and the 50.54-point margin was the week's biggest. Isaiah Likely, one-third of the Jeanty package, scored 26.9 in his first week in JMoney's lineup, and the trade's other two pieces, Emeka Egbuka (14.2) and Denzel Boston (12.1), added real points from the bench. That cushion meant Jordan could survive Jeremiyah Love posting 2.2 on a 13.06 projection.

Zoe's afternoon was a one-man show that the rest of the cast skipped. Jared Goff, her quarterback pickup from a week ago, delivered 28.94, and the rest of the lineup combined for just 40.2 of the week's lowest total. After last week's upset of Sonny, Ghostu-Spider SZN slips to 2-3 with 10% playoff odds and title odds that went from 2% to zero. Z² has shown she can win games she isn't supposed to; next week is about winning one she needs.

No Banner only HULK handled The fumblers 134 to 99.64, and Ramon's engine was, fittingly, a Bills quarterback: Josh Allen scored 30.5 on a 19.9 projection for the league's resident Chicago-to-Buffalo convert. Ramon could even afford to leave Matthew Stafford's 27.32 on the bench. Randy got a monster game from Jaylen Warren, 33.8 on a 15.86 projection, and still lost by 34.36. The fumblers have now dropped two straight after a 3-0 start, and their title odds cratered from 14% to 4%.

Sonny went into Kaushal's house as a slight underdog and won 137.6 to 118.34. Bucky Irving was the difference, scoring 30.5 on a 13.97 projection for The Horse is Hea. Habibsters got 29.2 from Puka Nacua, but CeeDee Lamb went from last week's 32.8 hero to 1.9 on a 15.46 projection, the week's second-biggest bust. Kaushal is 1-4 despite owning the league's fourth-most points (577.4), which is why the model still gives him 30% playoff odds.

The top of the table is a three-way tie at 4-1, sorted by points: No Banner only HULK (695), Team Pillbert (624.5) and The Horse is Hea (604.3). Ramon's 70.5-point lead in points scored has the model all in, pushing his title odds from 41% to 55%. The strange one is Alan: four straight wins, the week's top score, and his title odds still slid from 21% to 16%, while Sonny jumped from 11% to 18% and passed him. The fumblers hold the last playoff spot at 3-2 with 48% playoff odds, with Habibsters (30%), Dawgs (25%), Ghostu-Spider SZN (10%) and Counting or not Counting GV (1%) chasing.

The wire was busy, and nobody was busier than Randy, who dropped Trevor Lawrence for Deshaun Watson, then dropped Watson and picked Lawrence back up, a round trip that ended exactly where it started. He also cut Courtland Sutton, added Romeo Doubs, swapped Rams D/ST for Raiders D/ST, and replaced Tyler Loop with Matt Gay. Alan added and dropped Joe Mixon in the same week and also grabbed Keon Coleman and Odell Beckham Jr. Ramon picked up T.J. Hockenson and dropped the Bills D/ST, Mekhi added Malik Nabers for TreVeyon Henderson along with new defense and kicker swaps, Sonny cut Tony Pollard for Emanuel Wilson, and Jordan swapped Dalton Schultz for kicker Evan McPherson.

Week 6 brings the heavyweight bout: The Horse is Hea versus No Banner only HULK, two 4-1 teams, with Sonny and Ramon also facing off over the Hubbard-for-Rice deal that has given both sides nothing so far. Team Pillbert hosts The fumblers, which means Alan's four-game streak runs into Randy's two-game skid and the Javonte Williams-for-Stefon Diggs trade gets a live rematch. Zoe and Mekhi both need a win to stay in the playoff conversation, and Habibsters against Counting or not Counting GV is a battle of 1-4 teams where one of them gets to feel alive.

trade_watch.take: This one keeps getting uglier for Randy: Javonte Williams started and scored 13.2 for Alan, pushing him to 42 since the trade, while Stefon Diggs sat for a zero and is stuck at 6. The gap is now 36 points, and the two teams meet in Week 6.

Two weeks in and still zero lineup points on either side: Chuba Hubbard sat on Sonny's bench with 0 this week, and Rashee Rice has yet to score a point for Ramon. The two managers play each other next week, so somebody finally has an incentive to cash this in.

Jordan's depth-for-star bet looked even on paper and looks great on the scoreboard: Likely started and scored 26.9 in the first win of the season, and Egbuka (14.2) and Boston (12.1) added 26.3 more from the bench. Alan's prize, Jeanty, is already scoring for Mekhi instead.
Mekhi won the box score on day one, 28.8 from Adams and Jeanty to 15.8 from Jefferson, which backs up the paper read. Alan just doesn't care, because his team won the head-to-head by 35.22.

bios.1: The defending champion is 4-1 after Bucky Irving's 30.5 powered a 137.6-118.34 win at Habibsters. Sonny's title odds climbed from 11% to 18%, passing Alan's. Week 6 brings the HULK and a chance to claim the top spot.
bios.2: Randy started 3-0 and has now lost two straight, wasting a 33.8-point game from Jaylen Warren in a loss to the HULK. Title odds fell from 14% to 4%, though at 3-2 he still holds the fourth playoff spot with 48% odds. His quarterback spot made a round trip on the wire and ended up right back at Trevor Lawrence.
bios.3: Jordan is finally on the board, beating Zoe 119.68-69.14 for the week's biggest margin, with Isaiah Likely scoring 26.9 in his first week. At 1-4 with 1% playoff odds, the season is about building something. Kaushal's Habibsters come next in a battle of 1-4 teams.
bios.4: Alan has won four straight, posted the week's top score with 143.66, and beat Mekhi in the trade rematch despite losing the head-to-head of the deal. The model still trimmed his title odds to 16%, so Team Pillbert keeps winning without winning any respect. Randy's skidding fumblers come next.
bios.5: Mekhi won the trade box score against Alan and lost the game by 35.22, with Jayden Daniels' 32.26 and Christian Watson's 29.3 on the bench behind a negative day from Tyler Shough. At 1-4 with 25% playoff odds, the Dawgs need their lineup to match their talent. Malik Nabers is the newest addition.
bios.6: The two-time champ is 1-4 despite the league's fourth-most points, and CeeDee Lamb's 1.9 sank a week where Puka Nacua scored 29.2. Kaushal still has 30% playoff odds because the scoring is there. A matchup with Jordan is a must-win.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut is 4-1 with a league-best 695 points, 70.5 more than anyone else. Josh Allen led a 134-99.64 win over Randy, and the title odds jumped to 55%. Next up is a 4-1 showdown with Sonny.
bios.8: Zoe's rookie season hit a pothole: Jared Goff scored 28.94 and the rest of the lineup managed 40.2 in a 69.14-point loss. At 2-3 with 10% playoff odds, Ghostu-Spider SZN needs to bounce back against Mekhi. The upset win over Sonny proved the ceiling is real.
